text: Flutter 'Failed to build iOS app' under Xcode 16 is an umbrella for six different bugs. The umbrella message only tells you xcodebuild exited non-zero. Run with --verbose, grep for the first lowercase 'error:', and fix that. The four most common root causes: Flutter older than 3.24.4, Podfile still pinning iOS 11, a stale Pods plus DerivedData ModuleCache from the previous Xcode, or a plugin that hasn't shipped a Swift 6 release yet. Stop reaching for flutter clean first; it does not touch the iOS caches that are actually broken.

AndroidX conflict in a Flutter Android build means two halves of your dep graph disagree about which Android support library they use. Set android.useAndroidX=true and android.enableJetifier=true in android/gradle.properties, then find the legacy plugin with ./gradlew app:dependencies. AGP 8 turned Jetifier off by default for build speed, which is why this error is back on the front page.
